data.description:
## Description
**What**: Add Rule 6 (the fenced '## Test Intent' header with intent_id and catches_regression_where fields, plus a per-language syntax appendix with canonical Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and bash fixture examples) and Rule 7 (sibling-case rule, one-header-per-function constraint) to plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/behavioral-testing-standard.md.
**Why**: This file is the schema that every downstream test-writer surface (sc-3), reviewer dimension (sc-4), and consumer reference (sc-6) builds on. It is the walking skeleton of the epic.
**Scope**:
- IN: Rule 6 text; intent_id field accepting the 94ed stable-slug format or the 'UNTRACKED -- <rationale>' sentinel; catches_regression_where sentence-completion form; per-language fixture appendix (Python docstring fence, JS/TS block-comment fence, bash line-comment fence); Rule 7 sibling-case rule; one-header-per-function constraint; legacy-test exemption.
- OUT: Updates to consumer files (sc-6), test-writer surface prompts (sc-3), reviewer dimensions (sc-4). No hook or semgrep changes.

## Done Definitions

- behavioral-testing-standard.md contains a Rule 6 section whose text names the fenced '## Test Intent' header, the intent_id field, and the catches_regression_where field ← Satisfies: sc-1
- Rule 6 includes three canonical fixture examples, one each for Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and bash, each embedding the markdown-fenced header in that language's comment syntax ← Satisfies: sc-1
- Rule 6 states that legacy tests not modified in the diff are exempt from the header requirement ← Satisfies: sc-1
- behavioral-testing-standard.md contains a Rule 7 section that requires a sibling parameterized case or new sibling test function when adding coverage for an already-claimed intent_id, forbids appending to an existing test function, forbids a duplicate intent_id without an orthogonal scenario suffix, and limits each test function to one header ← Satisfies: sc-2
- unit tests written and passing assert that behavioral-testing-standard.md contains the Rule 6 header fields and the Rule 7 sibling-case constraints ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, Rules 1-5 in behavioral-testing-standard.md are present and textually unchanged so the diff shows only additive changes, the implementer having obtained explicit user approval for the safeguard-file edit per CLAUDE.md rule 22 before merging ← Satisfies: sc-2
- When this story is complete, every new or modified test file authored by this story carries a valid Rule 6 '## Test Intent' header, consistent with the dogfood property of sc-7 ← Satisfies: sc-7

## Considerations

- [Safeguard] behavioral-testing-standard.md is a SAFEGUARD file under CLAUDE.md rule 22; edits require explicit user approval and must not weaken any existing rule. Adding Rule 6 and Rule 7 strengthens the standard and must leave Rules 1-5 intact.
- [Dependency] intent_id format consumes the 94ed-f55c stable-slug manifest; external blocker, not an in-epic dependency. d566 ships only after 94ed publishes the slug format.
- [Dependency] a03c-d55e completion-verifier consumes Rule 6 headers for intent_id-to-test_artifact lookup; sequential external blocker, no in-epic dependency.
- [Coordination] d566 must ship before sibling 7f42-e41f to avoid concurrent edits to behavioral-testing-standard.md.
- [Dogfood] This story authors its own Rule 6 / Rule 7 unit tests; those test files must themselves carry a valid Rule 6 '## Test Intent' header, satisfying the sc-7 dogfood property on this story's own tests.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a test-writing sub-agent, I want Rule 6 and Rule 7 added to behavioral-testing-standard.md, so that every new or modified test declares a parseable intent-claim header and sibling-case structure
